reason: NONE. The first thing I noticed was the sachet format and the "200 mg" on the front, and my reflex is that 200 mg is really two capsules of 100 mg, so I would check the per-capsule number and the pill size before anything else. The sachets are great for flights, but a new brand with zero reviews means I cannot read the 1-star complaints about stomach upset or fake dosing, and I do not buy magnesium without hundreds of reviews.
objection: No reviews at all, so I cannot check what the 1-star reviews say about stomach issues, pill size or whether the dose is real. A QR lab report is nice, but it is the brand's own claim until real buyers confirm it.
would_change_my_mind: Several hundred verified reviews with a decent share of 1-star complaints I can read and find harmless, or a cheap trial size to test my stomach first.
